subject: Implementation timeline, SOW clarifications, and contract redlines for Intersys
messages:
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@intersys.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Baker <tbaker@intersys.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft SOW & DPA excerpt for implementation planning

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for the kickoff call last week — good alignment on the integration surface. Attached is our consolidated SOW draft (v2) with a few inline comments, plus an excerpt of our standard DPA referencing data residency obligations. Before we lock dates with our ops team, legal has asked us to confirm a few items:

- Whether Redwood can provide SOC2 evidence for the Dedicated option (we saw references to "audit logs and retention" but need a concrete retention period).
- Your standard clause for subprocessors and whether Redwood will accept Intersys-required subprocessors notification (30 days).
- Clarity on IP ownership for joint-developed connectors (Intersys prefers a license-back model).

Can you help route to the right people and let us know which items are likely to be redlines vs. negotiable? We need to finalize budget approvals by Nov 25 and would like a go/no-go for the timeline by then.

Thanks,
Elena

Attachments:
- Intersys_SOW_v2_redlines.docx (docx)
- dpa_excerpt.pdf (pdf)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@intersys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 10:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Draft SOW & DPA excerpt for implementation planning

Hi Elena — thanks for sending this over and for the clear asks. Looping in Marissa (contracts) and Vanessa (partner ops) to trade through legal points and the ops schedule. Quick notes up top: 

- SOC 2: Redwood can provide a SOC 2 Type II report; retention for platform audit logs is typically 90 days by default for Hosted and Dedicated customers, but we can offer 1 year for Dedicated with an addendum (affects pricing).
- Subprocessors: Standard notice is 30 days for major changes; full pre-approval is a tougher lift but we can scope a notification and opt-out for a short list.
- IP: We usually offer a license to use jointly-developed connectors with a perpetual, non-exclusive license back to Redwood for platform improvements. Happy to propose specific language.

Next steps: Marissa — can you propose redline language for the IP clause and the subprocessor notification? Vanessa — after legal thumbs-up, can you confirm an ops window (target week of Dec 15) and whether we can meet Intersys' preferred 2-week pilot? Elena — if you can flag which clauses Intersys considers deal-breakers, that will help prioritize.

Mateo
Sr. Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi all — reviewed the SOW and DPA excerpt. I attached a tracked-redline version of the SOW with three primary contract edits and comments inline. Highlights: 

1) Clause 4.2 (IP & Deliverables): Propose: "All pre-existing IP remains with the originating party. For jointly developed connectors, each party grants the other a non-exclusive, worldwide, royalty-free license to use, reproduce, and distribute the jointly developed software for purposes of operating and selling their respective services. Any improvements specific to the Redwood serving runtime will be governed by Redwood's standard contribution and upgrade policy." (see doc)

2) Clause 7.1 (Audit logs & retention): Clarify retention: "Redwood will retain operational audit logs for 90 days for Hosted usage; for Dedicated/Private deployments Redwood will retain operational logs for 365 days subject to additional fees and an SOW amendment."

3) Clause 11.3 (Subprocessors): Counter-proposal: "Redwood will provide notification of new subprocessors 30 days prior to onboarding and will provide a reasonable opportunity for Intersys to object. If Intersys objects, parties will discuss in good faith; Intersys' ability to prohibit a subprocessor is limited to substantiated security or regulatory concerns and must be raised within 15 days of notice."

Also added a short service-level table in the SOW with rollout milestones and acceptance criteria for the 2-week pilot.

Attachments:
- Intersys_SOW_v2_redlines.docx (docx) [tracked changes]

Marissa
Head of Legal Ops (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 20 Nov 2025 11:20:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Draft SOW & DPA excerpt for implementation planning

Marissa/Mateo — thanks for the quick review. A few responses from our side: 

- IP: Intersys cannot accept a perpetual license-back that allows Redwood to distribute joint connector code to third parties without Intersys consent. We propose a limited license to Redwood to operate the connector for Redwood-hosted customers and to incorporate non-Intersys-specific improvements into Redwood's internal runtime, but not to sublicense the Intersys-specific connector.
- Audit Logs: 365-day retention for Dedicated is acceptable but we need explicit encryption-at-rest and access controls specified in the SOW.
- Subprocessors: We need a written objection window of 30 days (not 15), and for high-risk subprocessors Intersys requires a prior written approval.

We redlined the DPA excerpt and attached comments (see dpa_excerpt.pdf). Also flagged two SOW acceptance criteria items that require more detail: failure-mode handling for rate-limited token spills, and rollback procedure in case of model performance regressions.

Please let us know if Redwood can accept these specific points or provide alternative mitigations. We are aiming to have a final SOW and DPA by Nov 25 to stay on our procurement timeline.

—Intersys Legal

Attachments:
- dpa_excerpt.pdf (pdf)
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Intersys Legal <legal@intersys.com>, Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@intersys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Nov 2025 16:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Draft SOW & DPA excerpt for implementation planning

Thanks — appreciate the clear feedback. Summary of where we can meet you and where we need to propose alternatives: 

- IP: We can accept a narrower license as proposed by Intersys for Intersys-specific connector code. For shared improvements that are generic to Redwood's runtime, Redwood requests the right to include non-proprietary improvements in platform releases; we will exclude Intersys-specific code from any sublicensing. Marissa will draft final language reflecting that split.
- Audit logs & encryption: Redwood confirms AES-256 encryption at rest for logs and role-based access controls; we'll add the exact controls in the SOW appendix. 365-day retention for Dedicated is okay as an optional add-on; Vanessa will provide a price delta.
- Subprocessors: We can extend the objection window to 30 days for high-risk subprocessors and provide prior written approval for those flagged as high-risk. For routine subprocessors, we keep 30-day notice with a 15-day objection period.

Action items:
- Marissa: send final redline reflecting IP carve and encryption language by Mon, Nov 24.
- Vanessa: provide Dedicated pricing delta and confirm Dec 15 pilot feasibility by Mon, Nov 24.
- Elena/Tom: confirm whether the rollback/acceptance criteria items are resolvable with the proposed failure-mode doc we shared (attachment: integration_sequence.png).

I'll prepare a DocuSign packet once we have the final redline. If Nov 24 timeline holds, we can still make Nov 25 procurement deadline.

Best,
Mateo
Sr. Partnerships Manager
Redwood Inference
